findings.evidence: Specifically investigated per this round's mission item #5 ('did the DefaultComponent.vue timing change introduce any visible delay or flash-of-wrong-theme before the kiosk shell mounts'). The round-3 commit (0680c45c4) moved theme resolution out of created() (previously synchronous) into beforeMount()'s `router.isReady().then(() => this.applyThemeFromRoute(...))` -- confirmed by reading the live file: created() (line 119-124) is now a no-op, `theme` stays at its data() default of 'frontend' (line 100) until the router's initial navigation promise resolves. Vue Router 4's `$route` before router.isReady() is `START_LOCATION_NORMALIZED` (path:'/', meta:{}), NOT yet the real matched URL -- confirmed this is the exact scenario the round-3 fix's OWN regression test simulates and asserts on: defaultComponentTrackingBootstrapGate.spec.js:187-207 explicitly asserts `expect(wrapper.vm.theme).toBe('frontend')` DURING the unresolved window (route meta:{}). Critically, that computed `isKioskRoute` (DefaultComponent.vue:114-117) ALSO reads `this.$route.path`, which is likewise still '/' (not '/kiosk/...') during that same window, so it evaluates false too -- meaning for a cold/direct load landing on a kiosk sub-route, the FIRST paint renders `theme==='frontend'` (template line 3: full FrontendNavbarComponent + FrontendCartComponent + FrontendMobileNavBarComponent + FrontendFooterComponent -- the public vitrine chrome) instead of the intended `kiosk-locked-shell`, until router.isReady() resolves and the reactive `$route` watcher (line 188-192) corrects theme to 'kiosk'. Before this round's fix, the same unresolved window produced theme='backend' instead (old code's created() also ran against the same unresolved $route) -- but the 'backend' branch is gated by `!isKioskRoute` (which was ALSO false in the old code for the same reason) and further gated by `logged` (false pre-auth), so the old flash rendered essentially nothing visible (an empty, unauthenticated `<router-view>` with no matched component). The NEW code's flash target ('frontend' theme) is visually substantial by comparison (a full public navbar/cart/footer), which is a content change in what briefly renders during that race, even though the underlying race itself (unresolved $route on cold load) is not new. Real-world exposure is narrow, not proven from the artifacts on hand: (1) none of the 7 fresh PNGs show it -- Playwright's snap() calls all settle after explicit waits, and a sub-frame race is not something a static post-settle screenshot can capture either way; (2) the tested entry route (kiosk idle, state 00) imports its top-level components SYNCHRONOUSLY specifically to avoid this class of bug (router/index.js comment: 'Le trio lazy-only provoquait des navigations ou l'URL changeait sans montage de vue... Voir tests/e2e/kiosk-spa-black-screen-guard.spec.js'), so router.isReady() likely resolves within the same microtask turn for that specific URL, before any repaint; (3) every subsequent state in this wave's tested flow (01-05) is an SPA-internal router.push from an already-mounted DefaultComponent, which does NOT re-enter this race (theme updates synchronously via the watch:$route on every post-boot navigation) -- so the actually-exercised flow in this wave is not exposed. The residual risk is a cold/direct load of a deeper, LAZY-chunked kiosk sub-route (e.g. a kiosk browser crash-recovery reload landing mid-order on /kiosk/waiting/:id, which IS lazy-loaded under the 'kiosk-shell' webpackChunkName) -- a real but comparatively rare trigger. No regression test exists for the kiosk-route case specifically: grepped tests/js/ for isKioskRoute/DefaultComponent -- only defaultComponentTrackingBootstrapGate.spec.js exists, and its round-3 test (line 187) only asserts theme stays 'frontend'/never 'backend' pre-resolution for a '/suivi/...' route; it never asserts what a '/kiosk/...' route renders during that same window.
findings.fix_hint: If this needs closing: either (a) special-case the pre-resolution default so a URL path starting with '/kiosk' (readable synchronously from window.location.pathname, independent of router state) suppresses the frontend theme branch even before router.isReady(), or (b) add a lightweight CSS-level safeguard (e.g. body init state hiding #app content until a data-theme-resolved attribute flips) so no theme branch paints before the router settles, or (c) at minimum add a regression test mirroring defaultComponentTrackingBootstrapGate.spec.js's pattern but for `/kiosk/...` paths, to make the current (narrow, unconfirmed-in-production) exposure explicit and trackable rather than silent.
